drug_identity.off_label_note: Extensively used extra-label in veterinary medicine for susceptible infections.

metabolism_and_clearance.extra_information: Extensively metabolized in the liver and excreted primarily as inactive metabolites in the feces and urine. Less than 20% is excreted unchanged in the urine.

organ_burden_logic.note: Minocycline is metabolized by the liver and excreted in feces and urine.

brain.evidence: Therapeutic concentrations can be found in CSF.

kidney.evidence: Excreted primarily as inactive metabolites in the feces and urine. Less than 20% is excreted unchanged in the urine.

timing_profile.evidence: Dog oral bioavailability ≈50%, half-life ≈4 hours. Cat PO bioavailability 62%, elimination half-life 6.3 hours. Plasma protein binding was 60% in cats.

_ddi_note: Can chelate divalent or trivalent cations.

drug_interactions.evidence: Can chelate divalent or trivalent cations and decrease the absorption of the tetracycline.
Concurrent use with minocycline may cause digoxin toxicity.
Significantly decreases the oral bioavailability of minocycline in healthy dogs.
Bacteriostatic drugs may interfere with the bactericidal activity of penicillins, cephalosporins, and aminoglycosides.
Tetracyclines may depress plasma prothrombin activity; patients on anticoagulant therapy may need dosage adjustment.

dosage_list.evidence: 5 – 10 mg/kg PO every 12 hours without food has been suggested.
10 mg/kg IV or PO once or twice daily for 30 days.

dosage_list.duration_note: Must be followed by a bolus of water or food
dosage_list.evidence: Practically, 50 mg/cat (NOT mg/kg) PO every 24 hours is recommended.

renal_dose_adjustment.note: Can be used in patients with mild to moderate renal insufficiency without dosage adjustment. Patients with oliguric renal failure may require dosage adjustment.

hepatic_dose_adjustment.note: More rarely, increases in hepatic enzymes and/or hepatotoxicity are possible.

effects_and_mechanisms.common_mechanism: Inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by reversibly binding to the bacterial 30S ribosomal subunits, thus preventing aminoacyl tRNA attachment to the ribosome.
common_extra_effects: inhibitory properties against the activity of matrix metalloproteinases

species_notes.dog: In dogs, administration without food has been recommended due to the impact of food on drug pharmacokinetics. IV administration should be done slowly over a minimum of 10 minutes.
species_notes.cat: Pilling should be followed by a bolus of water or food (at least 6 mL for cats). Dry pilling should not be performed due to the risk of esophageal strictures.

dog.evidence: IV injections of minocycline in dogs have caused urticaria, shivering, hypotension, dyspnea, cardiac arrhythmias, and shock when given rapidly.

cat.evidence: Oral minocycline can cause esophagitis and esophageal strictures, particularly in cats. Dry pilling should not be performed.

storage_and_forms.storage: Store oral preparations at room temperature in tight containers. Do not freeze oral suspensions. The injectable should be stored at room temperature (20°C-25°C [68°F-77°F]) and protected from light, moisture, and excessive heat.

section_1_2_10.highlights: Oral and parenteral tetracycline antibiotic; potential alternative to doxycycline. May be used in patients with mild to moderate renal insufficiency without dosage adjustment. Administration on an empty stomach is preferred. Adverse effects are most commonly GI-related.
section_1_2_10.indications: Used for the treatment of a variety of bacterial infections, particularly when doxycycline is unavailable. Can be effective against some doxycycline-resistant staphylococci. Not recommended for bacterial cystitis or prostatitis.
section_1_2_10.client_info: Oral minocycline works best when given without food. Do not give as a dry pill, especially in cats, as it may cause throat/esophageal ulcers. Do not give antacids, oral iron, or antidiarrheal medicine within 2 hours.
